result.summary: This PR moves several CNodeState fields (m_requested_hb_cmpctblocks, m_provides_cmpctblocks, fPreferredDownload/m_preferred_download) to the per-peer Peer struct, converting them to atomics so they no longer require cs_main. A final scripted-diff commit renames fPreferredDownload to m_preferred_download for consistency. The change also removes cs_main usage from a handful of call sites and adds a lock annotation to NewPoWValidBlock.
result.problem: CNodeState fields guarded by cs_main add unnecessary lock scope and complexity to net_processing.cpp, and the maintainers have a stated goal (issue #27502) of reducing cs_main's footprint to avoid lock contention and simplify reasoning about thread safety. This mainly affects P2P code maintainers who need to reason about locking correctness rather than end users directly.

open_concerns: dergoegge noted the previous cs_main-based version was 'a little easier to reason about' regarding the m_num_preferred_download_peers invariant, but treated this as a soft preference rather than a blocking issue; author explained tradeoffs and dergoegge did not push back further
resolved_concerns: mzumsande asked whether NewPoWValidBlock needs a !m_peer_mutex annotation since the compiler misses it due to a lambda; author agreed and added the annotation in a later commit
dergoegge's nit to scripted-diff the fPreferredDownload rename was implemented in the third commit

result.card: This PR moves several CNodeState fields (compact-block negotiation flags and the preferred-download flag) into the per-peer Peer struct as atomics, removing their cs_main dependency, as part of a broader effort (issue #27502) to shrink cs_main's scope in net_processing. It is purely an internal refactor with no consensus, protocol, or user-facing behavior change, and reviewers agree the change is 'fine/safe' (dergoegge) though one preferred the old locking's easier reasoning without insisting on a change. Review has been substantive: concept ACKs from davidgumberg and mzumsande, a code-review ACK from dergoegge, and a full ACK from w0xlt after the author addressed a missed lock annotation and a rename nit. The PR currently needs a rebase (labeled 'Needs rebase', mergeable_state dirty) and conflicts with several other open P2P PRs touching the same file. Priority within p2p is modest since the benefit is maintainability and lock-scope reduction rather than a user-visible fix or feature.
